title: A Botswana Incentive Trip Works Best With Small Camps, Shared Flights and an Early Plan
content:
A Botswana incentive trip is a fly-in reward safari for a company's top performers, usually six or seven nights moving between small camps on the Chobe River, in the Okavango Delta and in private concessions such as Khwai. It suits groups of roughly 8 to 40 guests and feels exclusive because Botswana keeps visitor numbers deliberately low.

The hard part for an HR or sales lead is not choosing Botswana but running it: tiny aircraft, 20 kg luggage limits, camps that hold a dozen tents and a winner list that changes until the last month. This guide covers group sizes, routes, flights, costs and timing, and explains how our corporate and incentive safaris team in Nairobi turns those constraints into a reward people talk about for years.

Quick Facts

  • Ideal length: 6 to 7 nights; 5 is the practical minimum
  • Typical group: 8 to 40 guests, split across small camps of about 8 to 12 tents
  • Gateways: Maun and Kasane, usually reached via Johannesburg
  • Camp transfers: Light aircraft such as the Cessna Grand Caravan, up to 12 passengers
  • Luggage: 20 kg per person including hand luggage, soft bags (checked November 2026)
  • Best months: May to October for game viewing; November to April for lower rates

Why Choose a Botswana Incentive Trip Over a Busier Safari Destination?

Botswana earns its place on an incentive shortlist because it feels private. The country's camps are small, many sit in concessions where only their own guests drive, and a group can spend a week seeing elephants, lions and wild dogs without queueing behind other vehicles at a sighting.

That sense of space is what a Botswana incentive trip sells to a sales team that hit its number. It also mixes water with land: boat cruises among Chobe's elephant herds, game drives in Moremi and, in the Okavango's wetter areas, quiet trips in a mokoro dugout canoe.

What a Botswana incentive trip does well

A Botswana incentive trip does three things well: real wilderness, a group kept together in camps where staff learn every name within a day, and set-piece moments: a sundowner on a sandbank, a bush dinner by lantern light, a scenic flight over the delta channels.

Where it is harder than East Africa

Be honest with your leadership team about the trade-offs. Botswana costs more per night than most of Kenya or Tanzania, every camp move involves a light aircraft, and the biggest venues for a 100-person conference are not in the bush. If your programme needs plenaries and breakout rooms, our Masai Mara incentive trip guide shows how Kenya handles larger numbers closer to a capital city.

How Many People Can a Botswana Incentive Group Include?

A single camp on a Botswana incentive trip typically sleeps around 16 to 24 guests in 8 to 12 tents, so groups up to about 20 can often book a whole camp. Between 20 and 40, the usual answer is two or three sister camps of the same standard that share an area and meet for evening events.

Taking a whole camp gives you control of the menu, the timings and the fire pit, and our guide to booking an exclusive use safari camp in Botswana explains how buyouts are priced and held. For bigger groups we keep every camp at the same tier, so no one feels sent to the "B" lodge.

Group sizeTypical set-upWhat to watch
8 to 12 guestsOne camp, often taken exclusivelySingle supplements if winners do not share
13 to 20 guestsOne larger camp or two neighbouring campsEnough vehicles so no one sits in a middle seat
21 to 40 guestsTwo or three sister camps, shared gala nightEqual standard across camps; staggered flights
40+ guestsKasane resort base with day trips into ChobeLess exclusivity; consider waves of departures

Rooming, partners and vehicles

Decide early whether winners bring partners. Ten winners with partners need ten doubles; ten solo winners need ten singles, each with a supplement. On a Botswana incentive trip we seat vehicles by friendship groups rather than seniority.

Which Route Suits a Five- to Seven-Night Reward?

The classic route runs from Kasane on the Chobe River to the Moremi area of the Okavango and on to the Khwai Concession, ending with a flight to Maun. It is the shape of our 7 day Chobe, Moremi and Khwai safari, which starts from USD 4,870 per adult on its trip page.

NightsBaseHighlights for the group
1 to 2Chobe riverfront, near KasaneBoat cruises among elephants and hippos, game drives in Chobe National Park
3 to 4Moremi area, OkavangoScenic flight in, floodplain game drives, mokoro where water levels allow
5 to 6Khwai ConcessionPredators, walking safaris and night drives, private bush dinner
Day 7Fly to MaunConnect to Johannesburg for international flights home

For a celebration feel, our 7 day Botswana celebration safari follows the same Chobe, Moremi and Khwai line with special dinners built in, and it adapts neatly to an awards programme. Our Okavango Delta vs Chobe comparison helps if you need to cut a region.

How Do Flights and Luggage Work for a Group?

Flights shape every Botswana incentive trip, more than any other detail. International guests usually connect through Johannesburg to Maun or Kasane, then hop between camps on light aircraft. Mack Air, one of the local operators, flies Cessna Grand Caravans carrying up to 12 passengers, so a group of 24 fills two planes.

Airlink and Ethiopian Airlines have added frequencies on Maun routes, according to a December 2025 Botswana Tourism Organisation update, which helps when winners fly in from different cities. On a Botswana incentive trip we often charter whole aircraft so the group moves and arrives together.

The 20 kg rule and how to handle it

On a Botswana incentive trip the luggage limit catches out corporate travellers more than anything else. Mack Air allows 20 kg per person including hand luggage, in bags no larger than about 30 x 35 x 70 cm, with soft bags preferred (checked November 2026). Send the rule with the winner announcement, and arrange to store business clothes in Maun or Kasane.

Visas and health paperwork

Many passport holders enter Botswana without a visa, but some must apply through the eVisa portal or an embassy. The Botswana government tourism visa page lists the documents and quotes 7 to 14 working days to process (checked November 2026). NHS Fit for Travel advises that a yellow fever certificate is required for travellers aged one or over arriving from a risk country, which includes guests coming via Kenya, and that the north, including the Okavango, carries malaria risk.

Can the Group Add Victoria Falls?

Yes. Victoria Falls is about 80 km from Kasane by road, according to the Botswana Tourism Organisation, so a Botswana incentive trip can open or close with a night at the falls: a guided walk through the rainforest, a sunset cruise on the Zambezi and a welcome dinner.

The falls sit in Zimbabwe and Zambia, so the group crosses a border and may need a separate visa for that country; check each passport before you commit. Spray and water volume are greatest after the rains, roughly March to May, and lowest late in the dry season. For a gala night with a stage and sound system, Victoria Falls and Kasane have larger hotels and conference venues than any bush camp.

How Much Does a Botswana Incentive Trip Cost Per Person?

A Botswana incentive trip typically costs from about USD 5,000 per person for a mid-range week to well over USD 15,000 at the top camps in peak season, before international flights. Season, camp tier, charter flights and private events drive the difference. The figures below are our estimates, not quotes.

TierEstimated cost per person per nightWhat it looks like
Mid-rangeAbout USD 500 to 900Comfortable tented lodges near park boundaries, shared activities
PremiumAbout USD 1,000 to 2,000Private concession camps, smaller vehicles, more included activities
Top tierAbout USD 2,000 to 4,000+Flagship camps, exclusive use, private guides and vehicles
ExtrasVariesCharter flights, gala dinner, gifts, Victoria Falls night, branding

Most camps on a Botswana incentive trip sell on a fully inclusive basis, so the nightly rate usually covers meals, activities, drinks and park or concession fees, which makes budgeting simpler than in many destinations. Ask what is excluded: premium spirits, laundry, gratuities and scenic helicopter flights often are. Green-season dates from November to April can lower camp rates noticeably.

Where the budget usually goes wrong

Three things blow the budget of a Botswana incentive trip: late winners after camps are full, unplanned single supplements and last-minute charters. Spare tents and an agreed release date with each camp prevent most of it.

When Is the Best Time for a Botswana Incentive Programme?

May to October is the safest window for a Botswana incentive programme. The dry season pulls wildlife to the rivers and lagoons, the Okavango floods are high in the middle of the year, and days are clear. July to October is the costliest and books out first, so popular camps need holding 12 to 18 months ahead.

November to April is the green season: hotter, with afternoon storms, but lush, full of newborn animals and migrant birds, and cheaper. A green-season Botswana incentive trip suits companies whose year ends in December. Our best time to visit Botswana guide breaks the year down month by month.

Making the Reward Feel Personal and Safe

The best moments on a Botswana incentive trip are small and well timed. A private sundowner on the Chobe at the end of the first day sets the tone, a bush dinner in Khwai can carry the awards, and a handwritten note in each tent from the CEO costs nothing yet gets mentioned for months.

For a formal awards night with staging, larger Kasane resorts with conference space, such as Cresta Mowana Safari Resort and Spa, can host the whole group in one room, something few bush camps can do. On a Botswana incentive trip, many groups save the final Kasane or Victoria Falls night for the gala and keep the bush days relaxed.

Safety planning matters as much as the fun. Remote camps are a flight from the nearest hospital, so every guest needs travel insurance with medical evacuation cover; see our notes on travel insurance. Brief guests on walking near camp after dark, malaria precautions and the guide's instructions on game drives, and share a single emergency contact sheet with your own duty manager.

Pre- and post-trip touches that lift a Botswana incentive trip

A short teaser campaign, a packing list matched to the 20 kg rule and a branded soft duffel bag all build anticipation before a Botswana incentive trip. If some winners want more, add a Cape Town stay or a few days in the Kalahari as a paid extension. Our guide to organising a group safari covers deposits, rooming lists and timelines, and the wider group safaris pages show other formats.

Insider Tips

  • Hold early: Put camps on provisional hold 12 to 18 months ahead for July to October
  • Charter smart: Charter aircraft for groups over about 10 so everyone travels together
  • Luggage first: Send the 20 kg soft-bag rule with the winner announcement
  • Passports: Collect nationalities early to check visas for Botswana and any Victoria Falls side trip
  • Spare tents: Keep one or two tents in reserve for late winners or a VIP guest
  • Gala venue: Stage the awards in Kasane or Victoria Falls; keep the bush nights informal

Frequently Asked Questions

How many days should a Botswana incentive trip be?

A Botswana incentive trip works best at six or seven nights: two on the Chobe riverfront, two in the Moremi or Okavango area and two in the Khwai Concession, with an optional Victoria Falls night at the start. Five nights is possible with fewer camp moves, but anything shorter spends too much of the reward in transit from Johannesburg.

How big can a Botswana incentive group be?

Most Botswana camps have roughly 8 to 12 tents, so a group of up to about 20 guests can often take a whole camp, while groups of 20 to 40 are usually split across two or three camps of the same standard that meet for shared dinners. Larger groups normally base the gala night in Kasane, where there are bigger resorts.

Do guests need a visa for a Botswana incentive trip?

Many nationalities can visit Botswana without a visa, but others must apply through Botswana's eVisa portal or an embassy, and the government quotes 7 to 14 working days to process an application (checked November 2026). Collect every winner's passport nationality early and confirm current rules on the official government site before booking flights.

What is the luggage limit on Botswana safari flights?

Light aircraft in Botswana usually allow 20 kg per person including hand luggage, in soft bags. Mack Air, for example, sets a 20 kg limit and a bag size of about 30 x 35 x 70 cm (checked November 2026). Tell winners early, and arrange storage in Maun or Kasane for business clothes or gala outfits.

When is the best time for a Botswana incentive trip?

The best time for a Botswana incentive trip is May to October, the dry season, when animals gather near water and the Okavango floods are high. July to October is the most expensive and books out first. November to April is the green season, with lower camp rates, lush scenery, afternoon storms and newborn animals.

Final Thoughts

A Botswana incentive trip rewards people with something rare: space, water and wildlife with hardly anyone else around. It asks more of the organiser, with small camps, small planes and strict luggage, but planned early it runs smoothly and feels far more personal than a resort.
